description: Mahāśivarātri, the 'Great Night of Śiva', observed on the 14th night of the dark fortnight of Phālguna/Māgha (Feb–Mar); all-night vigil (jāgaraṇa), fasting, Rudrābhiṣeka, bilva leaf offerings, and the chanting of 'Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya'; its association with Śiva's cosmic dance (Tāṇḍava) and the marriage of Śiva-Pārvatī are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Makara Saṅkrānti
description: The solar transition into Capricorn (Makara), marking uttarāyaṇa; celebrated across India with diverse regional names and practices (Pongal, Lohri, Magh Bihu, etc.).

title: Nāga Pañcamī
description: A festival honoring serpent deities (nāgas) on the fifth day of bright Śrāvaṇa; its observances, including milk offerings and snake imagery, vary regionally.

title: Navarātri
description: Navarātri (नवरात्रि / நவராத்திரி / നവരാത്രि / নৰরাত্রি / नवरात्री), the nine nights (nava-rātri) dedicated to the Goddess in her three guṇa-forms: Durgā (tamas, days 1-3), Lakṣmī (rajas, days 4-6), Sarasvatī (sattva, days 7-9). Autumn (Śarad, Sept-Oct) and Spring (Vasanta, Mar-Apr). Regional expressions: Durgā Pūjā (Bengal, pandals, immersion), Golu/Kolu (Tamil Nadu/Kerala, doll displays), Bathukamma (Telangana, flower stacks), Garbā/Dāṇḍiyā (Gujarat, circle dances), Mysore Dasara (royal procession), Ramlila (North, Rāma enactment), Ayudha Pūjā (tools/vehicles worship, day 9). Vijayadaśamī (day 10) = Dussehra (Rāma's victory) / Vidyarambha (initiation of learning). Fasting, devī-māhātmya recitation, kanya-pūjana (girls worshipped). ---

title: Oṇam
description: Oṇam (ഓണം), the state festival of Kerala, celebrated for ten days in the month of Ciṅgam (Aug-Sep). Commemorates the annual visit of Mahābali (Māvēli), the benevolent asura king, who was sent to Pātāla by Vāmana (Viṣṇu's dwarf avatāra) but granted a yearly return. Key elements: Pukkalam (floral rangoli), Oṇasadhya (feast on banana leaf with 20+ dishes), Vallam-kaḷi (snake boat races), Pulikkali (tiger dance), Tiruvaṭira (women's dance). The festival unites communities across religious lines. Glorified in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham and associated with the Tṛkkākkāra Vāmana Temple. --- A Kerala festival combining harvest commemoration with the mythological narrative of Mahabali and Vamana; its practices and narratives vary across communities and are represented here with attention to regional grounding.

title: Pongal
description: A Tamil harvest festival marking the sun's northward journey (uttarāyaṇa); its four days (Bhogi, Surya, Mattu, Kaanum) feature distinct regional practices and foods.

title: Rakṣābandhana
description: Rakṣābandhana (Rakhi), the festival of the protective bond between siblings, observed on the full moon of Śrāvaṇa (Aug); the sister ties a rakhi (sacred thread) on the brother's wrist, and the brother vows protection; its regional variations, historical narratives (Roxana-Poross, Draupadī-Kṛṣṇa), and contemporary practice are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāma Navamī
description: Rāma Navamī, the festival of Rāma's birth, observed on the ninth day (navamī) of the bright fortnight of Caitra (Mar–Apr); Rāma-pūjā, Rāmāyaṇa recitation, Rāmalīlā enactments, and the ceremonial wedding (Sītā-Rāma kalyāṇam) in South India; its observance in Ayodhyā, Rāmeśvaram, and Bhadrachalam are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ratha Yātrā
description: The chariot festival of Jagannātha at Purī, where the deities are taken in massive chariots to Guṇḍicā Temple; its scale, rituals, and participation are distinctive to Odisha.

title: Thai Pusam
description: The Tamil festival dedicated to Skanda/Murugaṇ on the full moon of Thai (Jan–Feb), observed with kavadi (burden-bearing), piercings, and processions; its regional prominence in Tamil Nadu, Malaysia, and Singapore is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ugādi
description: The New Year festival in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka, marking the first day of Chaitra; observed with ritual baths, new clothes, and the Ugadi pachadi (six tastes).

title: Baisākhī
description: The Punjabi harvest festival and Sikh New Year, commemorating the Khalsa's founding in 1699; observed with processions, kirtan, and community meals (langar). ---

title: Vaṭa Sāvitrī
description: A festival observed by married women for their husbands' longevity, centered on the banyan tree (vaṭa) and the Sāvitrī-Satyavān narrative; practices vary regionally.

title: Viṣu
description: Viṣu (വിഷു), the Malayalam New Year (Kolla Varṣam), observed on the first day of Meḍam (mid-April) when the Sun enters Meṣa Rāśi. The central ritual is Viṣukkaṇi (വിഷുക്കണി) — the auspicious first sight arranged the night before: a kaṇikonna (golden shower) flowers, rice, coconut, fruits, gold coins, mirror, and the Bhagavad Gītā or Rāmāyaṇa placed before Kṛṣṇa's image. Elders give Kaiṇeṭṭam (money gifts) to younger members. The Sādya feast includes viṣu-kaṭṭu (banana chips), māṅgā-caru (mango curry), and pāyaśam. Fireworks and the Viṣu-veḷḷa (boat race) at Aranmula. Marks the agricultural new year in Kerala. --- The Malayalam New Year in Kerala, marking the sun's transit into Meda Rāśi; observed with the Vishukkani (auspicious first sight), money gifts (kaineettam), and feasting.

title: Guru
description: A glossary entry for the term guru, representing its range of meanings without prescribing a single definition.

title: Mantra
description: A glossary entry for the term mantra, representing its range of meanings without prescribing a single definition.

title: Prasāda
description: A glossary entry for the term prasāda, representing its ritual and social meanings across traditions.

title: Annamācārya
description: Annamācārya (1408–1503), the earliest known composer of saṅkīrtana (devotional songs) in Telugu, dedicated to Veṅkaṭeśvara of Tirumala; his 32,000+ compositions (saṅkīrtanas) on copper plates recovered in the 20th century, his role in the Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition, and his influence on Carnatic music are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Appayya Dīkṣita
description: Appayya Dīkṣita (1520–1593), the Advaita Vedānta scholar and Śaiva devotee, author of over 100 works including the Siddhānta-leśa-saṅgraha, Śivārkamaṇi-dīpikā, and Khaṇḍana-khaṇḍa-khādya; his synthesis of Advaita and Śaiva Siddhānta, his debate with Vijayeन्द्र Tīrtha, and his role in the Śrīvidyā tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Caitanya Mahāprabhu
description: A 15th–16th century Bengali saint and ācārya, founder of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava tradition; traditional hagiography and historical scholarship are kept distinct.

title: Jīva Gosvāmī
description: A 16th-century Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava theologian, author of the Ṣaṭ-sandarbha and systematic expositor of Caitanya's teachings; traditional attribution is represented without historical conflation.

title: Kabīr
description: Kabīr (c. 1440–1518), the mystic poet-saint of the Bhakti movement, synthesizing Hindu and Islamic devotional traditions; his verses (bījak, sākhīs, śabdas) emphasizing nirguṇa-bhakti (devotion to the formless), the guru, and the critique of ritual orthodoxy; his influence on the Kabīr Panth and Sikh scripture (Gurū Granth Sāhib) is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kanakadāsa
description: Kanakadāsa (1509–1609), the Haridāsa saint-poet from Karnataka, composer of kīrtanas in Kannada dedicated to Adikeshava (Viṣṇu); his works (Mohanatarangini, Ramadhanya Charitre, Nalacharitre) emphasizing bhakti, social equality, and devotion over caste; his association with Udupi and the Krishna temple are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Madhva
description: Traditional dating assigns Madhva to the 13th century CE; scholarly dates vary. He is associated with Dvaita Vedānta through traditional and textual lineages; this record represents his tradition without ranking it against other schools.

title: Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar
description: Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar (1775–1835), one of the Carnatic trinity, composer of ~500 kṛtis in Sanskrit, known for his mastery of rāga, the navagraha kṛtis, the kamalamba navavarṇa kṛtis, and his use of Sanskrit sahitya with intricate rāga structures; his influence on Carnatic music theory is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita
description: Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita (1613–1697), the Advaita Vedānta scholar and poet, grandson of Appayya Dīkṣita; author of the Śiva-leśa, Śivalīlārṇava, and the satirical Kaliviḍambana; his role in the Śrīvidyā and Advaita traditions in South India is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nimbārka
description: A Vedānta ācārya traditionally associated with Dvaitādvaita (Bhedābheda) Vedānta; traditional dating and biography are kept distinct from historical scholarship.

title: Purandaradāsa
description: Purandaradāsa (1484–1564), the 'father of Carnatic music' (Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha), composer of 475,000+ kīrtanas in Kannada and Sanskrit; his systematization of music pedagogy (sarali, janta, alankara, geetam, swarajati, varnam), his devotion to Viṭṭhala, and his role in the Haridāsa movement are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāghavendra Svāmī
description: Rāghavendra Svāmī (1595–1671), the Dvaita Vedānta pontiff (Rāghavendra Maṭha, Mantralayam), known for his commentaries on Madhva's works and his reputation as a miracle-worker; his role in the Dvaita tradition, the Brindavan at Mantralayam, and his continued popular veneration are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmakṛṣṇa Paramahaṃsa
description: Rāmakṛṣṇa Paramahaṃsa (1836–1886), the 19th-century mystic of Dakṣiṇeśvar, devotee of Kālī, who experienced diverse religious paths (Śākta, Vaiṣṇava, Advaita, Islam, Christianity) and declared 'yato mat tato patha' (as many paths, so many ways); his disciple Vivekananda, the Ramakrishna Mission, and his universalist message are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmānanda
description: Rāmānanda (c. 14th–15th century), the founder of the Rāmānandī sect, a North Indian Vaiṣṇava tradition emphasizing Rāma-bhakti and the accessibility of devotion regardless of caste; his disciples included Kabīr, Ravidās, and Sena; his role in the Bhakti movement in North India is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmānuja
description: Traditional dating assigns Rāmānuja to the 11th–12th century CE; scholarly dates vary. He is associated with Viśiṣṭādvaita Vedānta through traditional and textual lineages; this record represents his tradition without ranking it against other schools.

title: Śaṅkara
description: Traditional attribution places Śaṅkara in the 8th century CE; scholarly dating varies and historical reconstruction remains distinct from hagiographical accounts. He is associated with Advaita Vedānta through traditional and textual lineages.

title: Śyāma Śāstri
description: Śyāma Śāstri (1762–1827), one of the Carnatic trinity, composer of ~300 kṛtis in Telugu and Sanskrit, known for his swarajatis, his kamakshi navaratna mālikā, his ananda bhairavi compositions, and his distinctive rhythmic structures (tāḷa); his influence on Carnatic music is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Śrī Aurobindo
description: Śrī Aurobindo (1872–1950), the nationalist, philosopher, and yogi who developed Integral Yoga (Pūrṇa Yoga); his works (The Life Divine, Synthesis of Yoga, Savitri), his concept of the Supermind, the descent of consciousness, the Ashram at Pondicherry, and the Auroville township are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sūrdās
description: Sūrdās (c. 1478–1583), the blind poet-saint of the Puṣṭimārga (Vallabha sect), composer of the Sūrsāgar (thousands of Braj bhāṣā poems on Kṛṣṇa-līlā); his depiction of Kṛṣṇa's childhood (bāla-līlā), the gopīs' love, and the philosophy of puṣṭi (grace) are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Tulsīdās
description: Tulsīdās (1532–1623), the composer of the Rāmacaritamānasa (Awadhi retelling of the Rāmāyaṇa), the Hanumān Cālīsā, and the Vinaya Patrikā; his role in popularizing Rāma-bhakti in North India, his founding of the Sankat Mochan Temple (Varanasi), and his influence on the Rāmānandī tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Tyāgarāja
description: Tyāgarāja (1767–1847), one of the Carnatic trinity, composer of ~24,000 kṛtis in Telugu and Sanskrit, mostly on Rāma; his pancharatna kṛtis, his devotion to Rāma, his life in Tiruvaiyaru, and his influence on Carnatic music pedagogy are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Vallabha
description: A Vedānta ācārya associated with Śuddhādvaita (Pure Non-dualism) and the Puṣṭimārga tradition; traditional dating and biography are kept distinct from historical scholarship.

title: Vālmīki
description: Traditional attribution identifies Vālmīki as the author of the Rāmāyaṇa; traditional attribution and historical biography are kept distinct in this record.

title: Swami Vivekananda
description: Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902), the chief disciple of Rāmakṛṣṇa, the founder of the Ramakrishna Mission, the exponent of practical Vedānta at the 1893 World's Parliament of Religions (Chicago); his synthesis of Advaita with social service, his call for 'man-making education', and his role in modern Hindu renaissance are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Vyāsa
description: Traditional attribution identifies Vyāsa as the compiler of the Vedas and author of the Mahābhārata; traditional attribution is not presented as modern historical certainty.

title: Advaita Vedānta
description: A Vedānta tradition represented separately from Viśiṣṭādvaita and Dvaita, with its own textual and interpretive history.

title: Nyāya
description: A philosophical tradition focused on logic, epistemology, and the means of valid knowledge (pramāṇa), with a distinct technical vocabulary.

title: Pūrvamīmāṃsā
description: A tradition focused on Vedic hermeneutics, ritual action, and the authority of the Veda as an instrument of valid knowledge.

title: Sāṃkhya
description: A dualistic philosophical tradition distinguishing puruṣa and prakṛti, represented here without reducing its technical categories to a universal summary.

title: Vaiśeṣika
description: A school of atomistic metaphysics and category theory, closely associated with Nyāya in later synthetic developments.

title: Vedānta
description: A family of traditions interpreting the Upaniṣads, Brahma-sūtras, and Bhagavad Gītā; its internal schools are represented separately.

title: Yoga Darśana
description: The philosophical school systematized in the Yogasūtras, distinct from the many modern and traditional uses of the term yoga.

title: Abhiṣeka
description: The ritual bathing of a deity or sacred object with water, milk, curd, honey, etc.; its materials, mantras, and occasions vary by tradition and Āgama.

title: Annaprāśana
description: The seventh saṃskāra, the first feeding of solid food, typically in the sixth month; its timing and food items vary by tradition.

title: Antyeṣṭi
description: The final sacrament or funeral rites, whose procedures and underlying eschatology differ across texts, regions, and communities.

title: Ārati
description: The waving of lights before a deity as the culminating offering in worship; its form, number of lamps, and accompanying hymns vary by tradition.

title: Arcana
description: The ritual worship of a deity through sequential offerings (upacāras), typically in temple or home shrine; its sequence and items vary by tradition.

title: Bhajan
description: A devotional song or hymn, often in vernacular languages, sung individually or in groups; its forms, languages, and musical styles are diverse across regions and traditions.

title: Cūḍākaraṇa
description: The eighth saṃskāra, the first haircut (tonsure), typically in the first or third year; its timing and rites vary by text and regional tradition.

title: Dhyāna
description: A contemplative practice term whose methods and aims vary across philosophical and living traditions.

title: Garbhādhāna
description: The first saṃskāra, the rite of conception or impregnation, prescribed in Dharmaśātra for the desire of progeny; its observance varies by text and tradition.

title: Havana
description: Synonym for homa, the fire offering ritual; represented here as a catalogue entry without duplicating the homa record.

title: Homa
description: The fire offering (homa/havana) in which oblations are poured into the sacred fire; its mantras, materials, and purposes vary by Vedic school and occasion.

title: Japa
description: A practice category involving repeated recitation in varied contexts; traditions differ in mantra, method and guidance.

title: Jātakarma
description: The fourth saṃskāra, the birth rite performed immediately after delivery; its mantras and procedures vary across texts and family traditions.

title: Karṇavedha
description: The ninth saṃskāra, the ear-piercing rite; its timing, method, and gender applicability vary across texts and regional customs.

title: Kīrtana
description: A form of devotional call-and-response singing, often accompanied by instruments; its structure, repertoire, and performance contexts vary across traditions and regions.

title: Nāma Saṅkīrtana
description: The congregational chanting of divine names, central to many bhakti traditions; its forms, melodies, and organizational structures vary widely.

title: Nāmakaraṇa
description: The fifth saṃskāra, the naming ceremony typically performed on the eleventh or twelfth day after birth; its timing and customs vary regionally.

title: Niṣkramaṇa
description: The sixth saṃskāra, the first outing of the child, traditionally in the fourth month; its observance varies by text and family custom.

title: Pañca Mahāyajña
description: The five great daily sacrifices—devayajña, ṛṣiyajña, pitṛyajña, bhūtayajña, manusyayajña—prescribed in Dharmaśāstra for householders.

title: Pañcāmṛta
description: The "five nectars" (milk, curd, ghee, honey, sugar) mixed as a ritual offering and later distributed as prasāda; proportions and additional ingredients vary regionally.

title: Prāṇa Pratiṣṭhā
description: The ritual installation of the life-force (prāṇa) into a temple image (mūrti), transforming it into a living embodiment of the deity; its elaborate procedures vary by Āgama tradition.

title: Pravacana
description: A scriptural discourse or sermon, traditionally delivered by a learned teacher; its content, language, and setting vary across traditions and audiences.

title: Pūjā
description: A broad practice category whose forms, meanings and procedures vary by tradition, place and community. This portal does not provide universal ritual instructions here.

title: Puṃsavana
description: The second saṃskāra, performed during pregnancy for the well-being of the fetus; its timing and procedure vary across Dharmaśāstra texts.

title: Samāvartana
description: The eleventh saṃskāra, the completion of Vedic studentship and return home; its observance marks the transition from brahmacarya to gṛhastha.

title: Saṃskāra
description: The sacraments or rites of passage marking life transitions, whose number, sequence, and content vary across textual and regional traditions.

title: Sandhyāvandana
description: A daily observance associated with the junctures of the day, whose specific mantras and procedures differ by Vedic school and family tradition.

title: Ṣoḍaśopacāra
description: The "sixteen offerings" (upacāras) in formal deity worship: invocation, seat, water, etc.; the exact list and sequence vary by tradition and Āgama.

title: Śrāddha
description: The ancestral offering rites whose procedures, timing, and eligibility vary across textual prescriptions and regional practices.

title: Sīmantonnayana
description: The third saṃskāra, the parting of the hair rite performed during late pregnancy; its observance varies by text and regional tradition.

title: Svādhyāya
description: The practice of self-study or recitation of one's Vedic branch; a niyama in Yoga philosophy and a daily duty in Dharmaśāstra traditions.

title: Tapas
description: A term for austerity, heat, or disciplined effort whose forms and purposes vary across Vedic, Yoga, and Purāṇic contexts.

title: Tīrtha and pilgrimage
description: A category for pilgrimage and sacred journeys whose meanings and practices vary by place and tradition.

title: Upanayana
description: The initiation ceremony conferring Vedic studentship, whose age, rites, and social applicability differ across textual and community contexts.

title: Vidyārambha
description: The tenth saṃskāra, the commencement of formal education, often coinciding with upanayana or performed separately; its rites vary by tradition.

title: Vivāha
description: The marriage sacrament whose rituals, mantras, and legal frameworks vary across textual prescriptions and regional customary practices.

title: Vrata
description: A category of vows or observances whose forms and meanings vary by region, text and tradition.

title: Yajña
description: A ritual category with different textual, historical and contemporary contexts; this portal does not provide universal performance instructions.

title: Āditya Purāṇa
description: The Āditya Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, focusing on the worship of Sūrya (Āditya), solar deities, and solar rituals; its overlap with the Saura Purāṇa and role in solar traditions is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Agni Purāṇa
description: The Agni Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in approximately 383 chapters, transmitted as a discourse of Agni to the sage Vasiṣṭha. Its encyclopedic scope covers cosmology (sarga, pratisarga), geography (dvīpa, varṣa), temple architecture and iconography (pratimā-lakṣaṇa), medicine (Āyurveda), polity (rāja-dharma), Dharmaśāstra topics (saṃskāras, vrata, dāna), and yoga. It preserves the Lakṣmī-kalpa and the Śiva-rātra sections. A key source for traditional Indian knowledge systems. ---

title: Ahirbudhnya Saṃhitā
description: The Ahirbudhnya Saṃhitā, a major Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra text, focusing on the Sudarśana cakra, the Nṛsiṃha mantra, the cakra system, and the esoteric rituals of the Pāñcarātra tradition; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Aitareya Āraṇyaka
description: The Aitareya Āraṇyaka, associated with the Ṛgveda, contains the Aitareya Upaniṣad and discusses the inner meaning of ritual; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Aitareya Brāhmaṇa
description: The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, associated with the Śākalya Śākhā of the Ṛgveda, provides ritual prescriptions and theological explanations; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Aitareya Upaniṣad
description: An Upaniṣad associated with the Ṛgveda, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Ajita Āgama
description: The Ajita Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, covering the four pādas with emphasis on the nature of Śiva as Ajita (unconquered), temple rituals, and the philosophy of Śiva-Śakti; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Akṣi Upaniṣad
description: The Akṣi Upaniṣad, associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, focuses on the nature of the eye (akṣi) as a symbol of knowledge and the means to realize the inner self through vidyā; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Aṃśumān Āgama
description: The Aṃśumān Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, focusing on the radiant (aṃśumān) aspect of Śiva as the source of all light and knowledge; its treatment of the solar symbolism in Śaiva theology is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Aṅka Āgama
description: The Aṅka Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, detailing the distinguishing marks (aṅka) of Śiva's various forms and the iconographic prescriptions for temple images; its contribution to Śaiva iconography is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Āpastamba Dharmasūtra
description: The Āpastamba Dharmasūtra, associated with the Taittirīya Śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, is one of the earliest Dharma Sūtras prescribing social, legal, and ritual norms; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Āraṇyaka texts
description: The "forest texts" bridging Vedic ritual and Upaniṣadic speculation; represented here as a category rather than individual texts.

title: Āruṇi Upaniṣad
description: The Āruṇi Upaniṣad, associated with the Sāmaveda, is a saṃnyāsa Upaniṣad discussing the renunciant's life, the praṇava (oṃ), and the nature of Brahman; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Atharvaveda Saṃhitā
description: The Atharvaveda Saṃhitā, the fourth Veda, containing hymns and prose for healing, protection, and domestic rituals, transmitted in Śaunaka and Paippalāda recensions; its textual structure is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Atharvaveda
description: A Vedic collection represented as a concise catalogue record. Interpretive and recensional differences require separate sourcing.

title: Auśanasa Purāṇa
description: The Auśanasa Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, attributed to the sage Uśanas (Śukra), focusing on dharma, polity, and the worship of Śiva; its role in Śaiva and Dharmaśāstra traditions is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Avadhūta Upaniṣad
description: The Avadhūta Upaniṣad, a saṃnyāsa Upaniṣad, presents the teachings of Dattātreya on the liberated state (avadhūta) beyond all social and ritual conventions; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Baudhāyana Dharmasūtra
description: The Baudhāyana Dharmasūtra, associated with the Taittirīya Śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, is one of the earliest Dharma Sūtras and includes the Baudhāyana Śrauta and Gṛhya Sūtras; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Madhva Bhagavad Gītā Bhāṣya
description: Madhva's Gītā Bhāṣya, presenting the Dvaita interpretation, emphasizing the fivefold difference (pañca-bheda), the hierarchy of souls, and the supremacy of bhakti to Viṣṇu; its distinction from both Advaita and Viśiṣṭādvaita is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nimbārka Bhagavad Gītā Bhāṣya
description: Nimbārka's Gītā Bhāṣya, presenting the Bhedābheda interpretation, reconciling difference and non-difference through the relation of whole and part; its unique synthesis is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmānuja Bhagavad Gītā Bhāṣya
description: Rāmānuja's Gītā Bhāṣya, presenting the Viśiṣṭādvaita interpretation of the Gītā, emphasizing bhakti as the supreme path and the role of prapatti (self-surrender); its distinction from Śaṅkara's interpretation is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Śaṅkara Bhagavad Gītā Bhāṣya
description: Śaṅkara's Bhagavad Gītā Bhāṣya, the earliest surviving commentary on the Gītā (c. 8th century), establishing the Advaita interpretation of karma-yoga, jñāna-yoga, and bhakti-yoga as convergent paths to liberation; its influence on all subsequent Gītā exegesis is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Śrīdhara Bhagavad Gītā Bhāṣya
description: Śrīdhara's Gītā Bhāṣya (Subodhinī), an influential Advaita commentary known for its clarity and systematic exposition; its influence on later Advaita Gītā exegesis is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Vallabha Bhagavad Gītā Bhāṣya
description: Vallabha's Bhagavad Gītā Bhāṣya (Subodhinī), presenting the Śuddhādvaita interpretation, emphasizing puṣṭi (grace) as the means to participate in Kṛṣṇa's līlā; its distinctive emphasis on the path of grace is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 1 — Arjuna Viṣāda Yoga
description: The first chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Arjuna Viṣāda Yoga), describing Arjuna's dejection on the battlefield of Kurukṣetra and his refusal to fight; its 47 verses set the stage for Kṛṣṇa's teaching; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 10 — Vibhūti Yoga
description: The tenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Vibhūti Yoga), enumerating the divine manifestations (vibhūtis) of Kṛṣṇa as the supreme being in all aspects of creation; its 42 verses reveal the divine glories; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 11 — Viśvarūpa Darśana Yoga
description: The eleventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Viśvarūpa Darśana Yoga), revealing Kṛṣṇa's cosmic form (viśvarūpa) to Arjuna, containing the entire universe within the divine form; its 55 verses present the supreme vision; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 12 — Bhakti Yoga
description: The twelfth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Bhakti Yoga), delineating the path of devotion (bhakti), the qualities of the devotee (bhakta), and the superiority of bhakti as the path to the supreme; its 20 verses are the heart of devotional yoga; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 13 — Kṣetra Kṣetrajña Vibhāga Yoga
description: The thirteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Kṣetra Kṣetrajña Vibhāga Yoga), distinguishing the field (kṣetra, the body) from the knower of the field (kṣetrajña, the self), and describing the nature of both; its 35 verses analyze the relationship between body and self; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 14 — Guṇa Traya Vibhāga Yoga
description: The fourteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Guṇa Traya Vibhāga Yoga), analyzing the three guṇas (sattva, rajas, tamas) that bind the self to the body, their effects, and the means to transcend them; its 27 verses reveal the nature of the guṇas; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 15 — Puruṣottama Yoga
description: The fifteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Puruṣottama Yoga), describing the cosmic tree (aśvattha) with roots above and branches below, and the supreme Person (Puruṣottama) who transcends both the perishable and imperishable; its 20 verses reveal the supreme Person; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 16 — Daivāsura Sampad Vibhāga Yoga
description: The sixteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Daivāsura Sampad Vibhāga Yoga), contrasting the divine qualities (daivī sampad) with the demonic qualities (āsurī sampad), and their consequences for liberation or bondage; its 24 verses contrast the two paths; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 17 — Śraddhā Traya Vibhāga Yoga
description: The seventeenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Śraddhā Traya Vibhāga Yoga), analyzing the three types of faith (śraddhā) — sāttvika, rājasika, tāmasika — and their expressions in food, sacrifice, austerity, and charity; its 28 verses analyze faith; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 18 — Mokṣa Saṃnyāsa Yoga
description: The eighteenth and final chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Mokṣa Saṃnyāsa Yoga), summarizing the entire teaching, distinguishing true renunciation from false, and declaring the supremacy of bhakti and surrender to the divine; its 78 verses provide the final synthesis; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 2 — Sāṅkhya Yoga
description: The second chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Sāṅkhya Yoga), containing Kṛṣṇa's foundational teaching on the immortality of the self (ātman), the nature of action (karma), and the practice of yoga; its 72 verses are foundational to the Gītā's philosophy; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 3 — Karma Yoga
description: The third chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Karma Yoga), expounding the yoga of selfless action (niṣkāma karma), the nature of svadharma, and the cosmic cycle of yajña; its 43 verses elaborate the path of action; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 4 — Jñāna Karma Saṃnyāsa Yoga
description: The fourth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Jñāna Karma Saṃnyāsa Yoga), describing the transmission of yoga through the guru-paramparā, the divine manifestation (avatāra), and the synthesis of knowledge and action; its 42 verses reveal the nature of true knowledge; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 5 — Karma Saṃnyāsa Yoga
description: The fifth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Karma Saṃnyāsa Yoga), comparing the path of renunciation (saṃnyāsa) with the yoga of action (karma yoga), establishing their essential unity; its 29 verses clarify the relationship between action and knowledge; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 6 — Dhyāna Yoga
description: The sixth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Dhyāna Yoga / Ātma Saṃyama Yoga), detailing the practice of meditation (dhyāna), the discipline of the mind, and the qualities of the true yogin; its 47 verses present the practical path of meditation; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 7 — Jñāna Vijñāna Yoga
description: The seventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Jñāna Vijñāna Yoga), revealing the nature of the divine (Bhagavān) as both the material and efficient cause of the universe, and the distinction between lower (aparā) and higher (parā) knowledge; its 30 verses reveal the nature of the supreme; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 8 — Akṣara Brahma Yoga
description: The eighth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Akṣara Brahma Yoga), describing the imperishable Brahman, the practice of remembering the divine at the time of death, and the two paths of departure (arcirādi and dhūmādi); its 28 verses reveal the path to the supreme; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gītā Chapter 9 — Rāja Vidyā Rāja Guhya Yoga
description: The ninth chapter of the Bhagavad Gītā (Rāja Vidyā Rāja Guhya Yoga), revealing the supreme secret knowledge (rāja vidyā) of the all-pervading divine, the practice of devotion (bhakti), and the inclusivity of the divine path; its 34 verses reveal the king of sciences; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhagavad Gita
description: A sample record for a future contextual guide to a text situated within the Mahabharata. No translation or quotation is reproduced here.

title: Bhāgavata Purāṇa
description: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa (Śrīmad Bhāgavatam), one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in twelve skandhas (books) and ~18,000 verses. Composed as a dialogue between Śuka and King Parīkṣit on the banks of the Gaṅgā. Skandha 1-2: creation, cosmology, and the avatāras; Skandha 3-4: Kapila's Sāṅkhya, Dhruva, Prahlāda; Skandha 5: Bharata, Ṛṣabha, cosmic geography; Skandha 6: Ajāmila, Vaivasvata, Nṛsiṃha; Skandha 7: Prahlāda, Nṛsiṃha; Skandha 8: Vāmana, churning of the ocean; Skandha 9: genealogies; Skandha 10: Kṛṣṇa's līlā (Vṛndāvana, Mathurā, Dvārakā); Skandha 11: Uddhava-gītā, Yadu dynasty; Skandha 12: future, Kali age, Māhātmya. Central to Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavism and bhakti traditions across India. ---

title: Bhārgava Purāṇa
description: The Bhārgava Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, attributed to the sage Bhṛgu, focusing on dharma, prāyaścitta, and the worship of Viṣṇu; its role in Dharmaśāstra traditions is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Bhaviṣya Purāṇa
description: The Bhaviṣya Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in four parts (Brāhma, Madhyama, Pratisarga, Uttara) and ~28,000 verses, narrated by Sūta to the sages at Naimiṣāraṇya. Known for its "future" (bhaviṣya) orientation — prophecies, royal genealogies of future dynasties (Maurya, Gupta, Harsha, medieval Indian rulers, and even British period references), the Sūrya-vaṃśa and Candra-vaṃśa lineages, the Sāyaṇācārya's solar worship, the Kṛṣṇa-līlā, the Tulasī-māhātmya, the Rāma-nāma-māhātmya, the Kāśī-māhātmya, the Gayā-śrāddha, and numerous vrata-kathās. The only Purāṇa with extensive historical/prophetic content on post-Vedic Indian dynasties. Controversial for its late interpolations; the Pratisargaparvan is considered a later addition. ---

title: Bimbāmbikā Āgama
description: The Bimbāmbikā Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, associated with the Goddess Bimbāmbikā (a form of Śakti) and the Śaiva-Śākta synthesis in temple worship; its unique Śakti-oriented perspective is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Brahma Purāṇa
description: The Brahma Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in ~10,000 verses, traditionally ascribed to Brahmā and narrated to the sages at Naimiṣāraṇya. Covers creation (sarga), the solar and lunar dynasties, the geography of Bhārata-varṣa, the seven dvīpas, the glory of the Godāvarī and other rivers, the Śiva and Viṣṇu kṣetras (Ekāmra, Purī, Koṇārka, Kāśī), the Purī Jagannātha temple, the Ratha-yātrā, and the Saura and Gāṇapatya traditions. Contains the Gautamī-māhātmya (Godāvarī pilgrimage) and the Koṇārka-māhātmya. Bridges Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, and Saura traditions; especially important for Odisha and Andhra temple mythology. ---

title: Brahma Sūtra Adhyāya 1 — Samanvaya
description: The first adhyāya (chapter) of the Brahma Sūtra (Samanvaya), consisting of four pādas and 134 sūtras, harmonizing the diverse Upaniṣadic statements to establish that Brahman is the sole cause of the universe; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Brahma Sūtra Adhyāya 2 — Avirodha
description: The second adhyāya of the Brahma Sūtra (Avirodha), consisting of four pādas and 157 sūtras, refuting objections from other schools (Sāṃkhya, Yoga, Vaiśeṣika, Buddhist, Jain) and showing the consistency of the Vedānta doctrine; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Brahma Sūtra Adhyāya 3 — Sādhana
description: The third adhyāya of the Brahma Sūtra (Sādhana), consisting of four pādas and 186 sūtras, discussing the means (sādhana) to realize Brahman, including meditation (upāsanā), ethics, and the path of knowledge; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Brahma Sūtra Adhyāya 4 — Phala
description: The fourth adhyāya of the Brahma Sūtra (Phala), consisting of four pādas and 113 sūtras, describing the fruit (phala) of knowledge — liberation (mokṣa), the state of the liberated, and the fate of the knower of Brahman; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Madhva Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya
description: Madhva's Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya, the Dvaita commentary on the Brahma Sūtra, establishing the fivefold eternal difference (pañca-bheda) and Viṣṇu as the supreme independent reality; its refutation of Advaita and Viśiṣṭādvaita is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nimbārka Vedānta Pārijāta Saurabha
description: Nimbārka's Vedānta Pārijāta Saurabha, the Bhedābheda commentary on the Brahma Sūtra, establishing difference-and-non-difference with Kṛṣṇa as the supreme reality; its unique position between dualism and non-dualism is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Prakāśātman Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya
description: Prakāśātman's Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya (Pancapadika), a detailed Advaita commentary elaborating on the first five sūtras of the Brahma Sūtra; its analysis of the categories of error (bhrama) is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmānuja Śrī Bhāṣya on Brahma Sūtra
description: Rāmānuja's Śrī Bhāṣya, the principal Viśiṣṭādvaita commentary on the Brahma Sūtra, establishing qualified non-duality with Viṣṇu as the supreme Brahman qualified by conscious souls and matter; its refutation of Advaita and its systematic exposition of viśiṣṭādvaita are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Śaṅkara Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya
description: Śaṅkara's Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya, the earliest surviving and most influential commentary on the Brahma Sūtra, establishing the Advaita (non-dual) interpretation; its systematic exposition of Brahman as non-dual, the illusory nature of the world (māyā), and the identity of ātman and Brahman is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sureśvara Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya
description: Sureśvara's Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad Bhāṣya Vārtika), the direct disciple of Śaṅkara, providing a detailed Vārtika on Śaṅkara's Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya; its elaboration of Advaita arguments is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Vācaspati Miśra Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya
description: Vācaspati Miśra's Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya (Bhāmatī), a sub-commentary on Śaṅkara's Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya, establishing the Bhāmatī school of Advaita and its theory of avidyā; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Vallabha Anubhāṣya
description: Vallabha's Anubhāṣya, the Śuddhādvaita commentary on the Brahma Sūtra, establishing pure non-duality with Kṛṣṇa as the supreme Brahman and the path of grace (puṣṭi-mārga); its critique of māyā-vāda is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Brahma Sūtra
description: The Brahma Sūtra (Vedānta Sūtra) of Bādarāyaṇa, the foundational text of Vedānta darśana, in four adhyāyas and 555 sūtras; its systematic inquiry into brahman, the reconciliation of Upaniṣadic statements, and its role as the prasthāna-traya (with Upaniṣads and Bhagavad Gītā) are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Brahma Upaniṣad
description: The Brahma Upaniṣad, associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, focuses on the nature of Brahman, the self, and the means to liberation through knowledge and meditation; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Brahmayāmala Tantra
description: The Brahmayāmala Tantra, a major Śākta Tantra in 21 chapters, focusing on the worship of the Goddess as Brahmayāmala, the cakra system, and the Kaula initiation; its detailed ritual prescriptions are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Brāhmaṇa texts
description: The ritual commentaries attached to the Vedic Saṃhitās, explaining sacrificial procedures and their symbolic meanings; represented here as a category rather than individual texts.

title: Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa
description: The Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in four parts (prakriyā, anuṣaṅga, upodghāta, upasaṃhāra) and ~12,000 verses. Details the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), creation cycles, geography of the seven dvīpas, the Aṣṭādaśa-śakti-pīṭhas (eighteen Goddess shrines), and the Lalitopākhyāna (narrative of Lalitā Tripurasundarī) in the Uttarārdha. Contains the Āditya-hṛdaya, the Navagraha-stotras, and detailed pilgrimage (tīrtha) sections for Kāñcī, Śrīśaila, and other Śākta sites. Closely related to the Vāyu Purāṇa; together they preserve the Āditya and Śaiva-Śākta cosmologies. Key for Śākta tradition and South Indian temple mythology. ---

title: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad
description: The longest Upaniṣad, associated with the Śukla Yajurveda, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Bṛhaspati Smṛti
description: The Bṛhaspati Smṛti, a Dharmaśāstra text attributed to Bṛhaspati, focusing on vyavahāra (legal procedure), courts, evidence, and civil law; its influence on the Indian legal tradition and medieval dharma digests is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Chandaḥsūtra
description: The Chandaḥsūtra of Piṅgala is the foundational text of the Vedāṅga of metre (chandas), presenting the combinatorial analysis of Vedic and classical metres; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Chāndogya Brāhmaṇa
description: The Chāndogya Brāhmaṇa (the first part of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad's textual complex), associated with the Kauthuma Śākhā of the Sāmaveda, contains the Chāndogya Upaniṣad; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Chāndogya Upaniṣad
description: One of the longest Upaniṣads, associated with the Sāmaveda, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Cintya Āgama
description: The Cintya Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, focusing on the jñāna pāda and the contemplative (cintya) knowledge of Śiva as the supreme consciousness; its treatment of the thirty-six tattvas and the path of knowledge is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa
description: The Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa (Śrī Devī Bhāgavatam), a major Śākta Mahāpurāṇa in 12 skandhas and ~18,000 verses, modeled on the Bhāgavata Purāṇa's structure but centered on the Goddess. Skandha 1: creation, the Goddess as śakti; Skandha 2-3: the Devī's forms, the battle with Mahiṣāsura; Skandha 4: the Devī-gītā (the Goddess's teaching on jñāna, yoga, bhakti); Skandha 5: the Śākta cosmology, the Śrī-cakra, the nine nityās; Skandha 6: the Kālī-krama, the ten Mahāvidyās; Skandha 7: the Navarātrī vrata, the Caṇḍī-pāṭha procedure; Skandha 8-9: the glories of Śākta pīṭhas (Kāmākhyā, Kālikā, Tārāpīṭha); Skandha 10-11: the Rāma and Kṛṣṇa narratives retold from the Śākta perspective; Skandha 12: liberation through Devī-bhakti. The primary text for the Devī-gītā and Śākta theology, influential in Bengal and Assam. --- A major Śākta Purāṇa centered on the Goddess; represented here as a catalogue entry without reproducing translations.

title: Dīpta Āgama
description: The Dīpta Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, known for its treatment of the caryā pāda (conduct) and the radiant (dīpta) manifestation of Śiva in the world; its emphasis on the guru-śiṣya paramparā and the initiation lineage is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Dvijaja Āgama
description: The Dvijaja Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, associated with the twice-born (dvija) tradition of Śaiva initiation and the transmission of mantras through the guru-śiṣya lineage; its emphasis on dīkṣā is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Garbha Upaniṣad
description: The Garbha Upaniṣad, associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, describes the development of the embryo, the constitution of the body, and the relationship between the physical body and the subtle self; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Garga Purāṇa
description: The Garga Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, attributed to the sage Garga, focusing on astrology (jyotiṣa), omens, and the worship of Kṛṣṇa; its astronomical content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Garuḍa Purāṇa
description: The Garuḍa Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in ~19,000 verses, narrated by Garuḍa to Kaśyapa (or Viṣṇu to Garuḍa). Two main parts: Pūrvakhanda (Ācāra-kāṇḍa, Dharma-kāṇḍa, Preta-kāṇḍa) and Uttarakhanda (Brahma-kāṇḍa). Covers Viṣṇu worship, saṃskāras, vrata, dāna, temple construction, iconography, gemology (ratna-śāstra), astrology, medicine (Āyurveda), the afterlife journey (pretakalpā), the realms of Yama, funeral rites (antyeṣṭi), śrāddha, and the path to liberation through Viṣṇu-bhakti. Authoritative for death rituals and śrāddha procedures across Hindu traditions. ---

title: Gautama Dharmasūtra
description: The Gautama Dharmasūtra, associated with the Sāmaveda, is an early Dharma Sūtra presenting legal, social, and ritual norms; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Gopatha Brāhmaṇa
description: The Gopatha Brāhmaṇa, the only Brāhmaṇa of the Atharvaveda (associated with the Śaunaka and Paippalāda Śākhās), provides ritual instructions and explanations specific to Atharvan practice; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Gṛhya Sūtra
description: The Gṛhya Sūtras, the Vedāṅga texts of domestic rites (saṃskāras): marriage (vivāha), conception (garbhādhāna), birth (jātakarma), naming (nāmakaraṇa), first feeding (annaprāśana), tonsure (cūḍākaraṇa), initiation (upanayana), marriage, and funeral (antyeṣṭi); their relationship to Śrauta Sūtras and Dharma Sūtras is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Haṃsa Upaniṣad
description: The Haṃsa Upaniṣad, associated with the Śukla Yajurveda, teaches the Haṃsa-vidyā (the knowledge of the inner swan/breath) and the identity of the individual self with the supreme; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Harivaṃśa
description: The Harivaṃśa (Lineage of Hari), an appendix (khila) to the Mahābhārata in three books, detailing the lineage of Kṛṣṇa, his childhood in Vraja, and the history of the Yādava dynasty; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Īśā Upaniṣad
description: A short Upaniṣadic text represented here through an original catalogue description, without reproducing a translation.

title: Jabāla Upaniṣad
description: The Jabāla Upaniṣad (Jabala Upanishad), associated with the Ṛgveda, discusses prāṇa, the nature of the self, and the path to liberation; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Jaiminīya Āraṇyaka
description: The Jaiminīya Āraṇyaka, associated with the Jaiminīya Śākhā of the Sāmaveda, contains the Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Bṛhadāraṇyaka and related forest texts; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa
description: The Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa (also Talavakāra Brāhmaṇa), associated with the Jaiminīya/Talavakāra Śākhā of the Sāmaveda, contains ritual prescriptions and theological explanations; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Jayākhya Saṃhitā
description: The Jayākhya Saṃhitā, a major Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra text in 33 chapters, expounding the five forms of Viṣṇu (para, vyūha, vibhava, antaryāmin, arcā), the fivefold worship (pañcakāla), and the philosophy of Viṣṇu as supreme; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Jyotiṣa Vedāṅga
description: The Jyotiṣa Vedāṅga (Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa) attributed to Lagadha is the foundational text of the Vedāṅga of astronomy and calendrical science, used for determining ritual times; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kaivalya Upaniṣad
description: The Kaivalya Upaniṣad, associated with the Atharvaveda, is a Śaiva-oriented Upaniṣad describing the attainment of kaivalya (liberation) through devotion to Śiva and knowledge of the ātman; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kālikā Purāṇa
description: The Kālikā Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, a Śākta text focusing on the worship of Kālī, the ten Mahāvidyās, and the ritual practices of Śākta traditions in Kamarupa (Assam); its tantric orientation is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kāmika Āgama
description: The Kāmika Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, covering all four pādas (jñāna, yoga, kriyā, caryā) with detailed ritual instructions for temple construction, daily worship, and festivals; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kapila Purāṇa
description: The Kapila Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, attributed to the sage Kapila, focusing on Sāṅkhya philosophy, the worship of Viṣṇu, and the glory of the Gangā; its philosophical orientation is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Karaṇa Āgama
description: The Karaṇa Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, detailing the kriyā pāda with emphasis on temple rituals, the consecration of liṅgas, and the daily worship sequence (nitya-pūjā); its architectural and iconographic prescriptions are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kaṭha Āraṇyaka
description: The Kaṭha Āraṇyaka, associated with the Kaṭha Śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, contains the Kaṭha Upaniṣad and related ritual and philosophical material; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kaṭha Upaniṣad
description: An Upaniṣad structured as a dialogue between Naciketas and Yama, represented here through an original catalogue description without reproducing translations.

title: Kātyāyana Smṛti
description: The Kātyāyana Smṛti, a Dharmaśāstra text attributed to Kātyāyana, focusing on vyavahāra, women's property rights (strīdhana), and inheritance law; its influence on later dharma digests (Mitākṣarā, Dāyabhāga) is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa
description: The Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa, associated with the Bāṣkala Śākhā of the Ṛgveda, contains ritual prescriptions and theological explanations; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad
description: The Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad (also Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa Upaniṣad), associated with the Ṛgveda, discusses prāṇa, the nature of the self, and the path to liberation; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kena Upaniṣad
description: A short Upaniṣadic text focused on the nature of Brahman and the limits of empirical knowledge, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Kiraṇa Āgama
description: The Kiraṇa Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, known for its detailed treatment of dīkṣā (initiation), the nature of the soul (paśu), and the removal of mala; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kulārṇava Tantra
description: The Kulārṇava Tantra, a major Śākta Tantra in 17 chapters, expounding the Kaula tradition, the worship of Kuleśvarī, the cakra system, and the guru-śiṣya relationship; its synthesis of tantric and Vedic elements is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Kūrma Purāṇa
description: The Kūrma Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in two parts (Pūrvabhāga and Uttarabhāga) and ~17,000 verses, narrated by Kūrma (Viṣṇu's tortoise avatar) to the sages at Naimiṣāraṇya. Pūrvabhāga: creation, the four puruṣārthas (dharma, artha, kāma, mokṣa), the glory of the Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-hṛdaya, the unity of Śiva and Viṣṇu, the ṛṣi genealogies; Uttarabhāga: the Īśvara-gītā (Śiva's teaching on yoga and jñāna), the Vyāsa-gītā, the Śiva-gītā, pilgrimage to Kāśī, Prayāga, Gayā, and the Śiva kṣetras. A synthesis text emphasizing Śiva-Viṣṇu non-difference (abheda) and the yoga of knowledge and devotion. ---

title: Lakulīśa Pāśupata Sūtra
description: The Lakulīśa Pāśupata Sūtra, the foundational text of the Pāśupata Śaiva tradition founded by Lakulīśa, outlining the five categories (kārana, kārya, yoga, vidhi, duḥkhānta) and the path of the Pāśupata ascetic; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Lalitā Āgama
description: The Lalitā Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, associated with the playful (lalita) aspect of Śiva-Śakti union, integrating Śaiva and Śākta ritual streams in the worship of the Divine Couple; its synthesis orientation is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Liṅga Purāṇa
description: The Liṅga Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in ~11,000 verses and two parts (Pūrvabhāga and Uttarabhāga). Pūrvabhāga: the origin of the liṅga (liṅgodbhava), the glory of the liṅga, the twenty-eight Śaiva Āgamas, the five faces of Śiva (Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa, Īśāna), the eight forms (aṣṭamūrti), the twelve jyotirliṅgas; Uttarabhāga: the Liṅga-gītā (Śiva's teaching to the sages), the story of Dhruva, the Puṣkara-māhātmya, the glory of Kāśī, the Śiva-rātra vrata, the rites of liṅga-pratiṣṭhā and daily worship (nitya-pūjā). The definitive textual authority for liṅga worship in Śaiva temple tradition. ---

title: Mahābhārata Ādi Parva
description: The first book (Ādi Parva) of the Mahābhārata, containing the origins of the Kuru dynasty, the birth of the Pāṇḍavas and Kauravas, the game of dice, and the exile of the Pāṇḍavas; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Anuśāsana Parva
description: The thirteenth book (Anuśāsana Parva) of the Mahābhārata, continuing Bhīṣma's teachings on dharma, varṇa, āśrama, and the glory of Viṣṇu; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Āśramavāsika Parva
description: The fourteenth book (Āśramavāsika Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the Pāṇḍavas' retirement to the forest, Dhṛtarāṣṭra's death, and the end of the Kuru elders; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Bhīṣma Parva
description: The sixth book (Bhīṣma Parva) of the Mahābhārata, containing the first ten days of the Kurukṣetra war under Bhīṣma's command, including the Bhagavad Gītā; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Droṇa Parva
description: The seventh book (Droṇa Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the five days of war under Droṇa's command, including the deaths of Abhimanyu and Droṇa; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva
description: The eighth book (Karṇa Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the two days of war under Karṇa's command and his final duel with Arjuna; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Mahāprasthānika Parva
description: The sixteenth book (Mahāprasthānika Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the Pāṇḍavas' great journey (mahāprasthāna) toward the Himalayas and their successive falls; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Mausala Parva
description: The fifteenth book (Mausala Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the destruction of the Yādava clan through mutual slaughter (mausala) and Kṛṣṇa's departure; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Sabhā Parva
description: The second book (Sabhā Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the assembly hall (sabhā) of Yudhiṣṭhira, the Rājasūya sacrifice, and the fateful game of dice; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Śānti Parva
description: The twelfth book (Śānti Parva) of the Mahābhārata, the longest book, containing Bhīṣma's teachings on rājadharma, āpad-dharma, and mokṣa from his bed of arrows; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Sauptika Parva
description: The tenth book (Sauptika Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the night raid (sauptika) by Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman on the sleeping Pāṇḍava army; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Śalya Parva
description: The ninth book (Śalya Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the final day of war under Śalya's command, the mace duel between Bhīma and Duryodhana, and the end of the war; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Strī Parva
description: The eleventh book (Strī Parva) of the Mahābhārata, depicting the lamentations of the women (strī) after the war, including Gandhārī's curse and the grief of the widows; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Svargārohaṇa Parva
description: The seventeenth book (Svargārohaṇa Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing Yudhiṣṭhira's final ascent to heaven (svarga) and the resolution of the epic's central tensions; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva
description: The fifth book (Udyoga Parva) of the Mahābhārata, detailing the preparations for war (udyoga), the failed peace missions, and the marshalling of armies on both sides; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Vana Parva
description: The third book (Vana Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the Pāṇḍavas' twelve-year exile in the forest (vana), their encounters with sages, and the Nala-Damayantī episode; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahābhārata Virāṭa Parva
description: The fourth book (Virāṭa Parva) of the Mahābhārata, describing the Pāṇḍavas' thirteenth year of exile incognito at the court of King Virāṭa; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mahabharata
description: A sample record for a future guide to the Mahābhārata and its textual traditions. No translation or quotation is reproduced here.

title: Maitrāyaṇīya Āraṇyaka
description: The Maitrāyaṇīya Āraṇyaka, associated with the Maitrāyaṇīya Śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, contains the Maitrī Upaniṣad and related forest-text material; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Maitrī Upaniṣad
description: The Maitrī Upaniṣad, associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda (Maitrāyaṇīya Śākhā), presents a dialogue between King Bṛhadratha and Sage Śākāyanya on the nature of the self and the means to liberation; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Makuṭa Āgama
description: The Makuṭa Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, focusing on the crown (makuṭa) of Śiva as the symbol of supreme sovereignty and the coronation rites of the liṅga; its royal and ritual symbolism is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mānava Purāṇa
description: The Mānava Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, attributed to Manu, focusing on dharma, the four āśramas, and the worship of Viṣṇu; its role in Dharmaśāstra traditions is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad
description: The shortest principal Upaniṣad, focused on the syllable Oṃ and the four states of consciousness, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Manu Smṛti
description: The Manusmṛti (Mānava Dharmaśāstra), the most authoritative Dharmaśāstra text in twelve chapters, covering varṇa, āśrama, rājadharma, vyavahāra, prāyaścitta, and the rules of daily conduct; its influence on Hindu law and social organization is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa
description: The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in 137 chapters and ~9,000 verses, narrated as a dialogue between the sage Mārkaṇḍeya and Jaimini. Chapters 1-42: cosmology, creation, genealogies, the manvantaras; Chapters 43-80: the glory of the Sun (Sūrya), the legend of King Harishchandra; Chapters 81-93: the Devī Māhātmya (Durgā Saptashatī / Caṇḍī-pāṭha) — the Goddess's battles against Madhu-Kaiṭabha, Mahiṣāsura, and Śumbha-Niśumbha, the foundation of Śākta worship and Navarātrī; Chapters 94-137: the story of Dama, the glories of the Goddess, liberation through Devī-bhakti. The primary textual source for the Caṇḍī-pāṭha recited during Durgā Pūjā and Navarātrī across India, especially Bengal. ---

title: Matsya Purāṇa (Upapurāṇa)
description: The Matsya Upapurāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, distinct from the Mahāpurāṇa Matsya Purāṇa, focusing on the Matsya avatar of Viṣṇu, temple architecture, and vrata; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Matsya Purāṇa
description: The Matsya Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in ~14,000 verses and 291 chapters, narrated by Matsya (Viṣṇu's fish avatar) to Manu. Covers the Matsya avatāra and the flood legend, the seven Manus, royal genealogies (Sūryavaṃśa, Candravaṃśa), the five characteristics of a Purāṇa (pañca-lakṣaṇa), temple architecture (vāstu-śāstra: prāsāda, maṇḍapa, gopura, pratimā-lakṣaṇa), iconography of major deities, vrata rituals (Śivarātri, Caturmāsya, Ekādaśī), the Śrāddha-vidhi, the Prayāga-māhātmya, the Kāśī-māhātmya, and the Narmadā-māhātmya. The earliest Purāṇic source for Hindu temple architecture and iconography. ---

title: Mṛgendra Āgama
description: The Mṛgendra Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, focusing on the philosophy of Śiva, the nature of the soul (paśu), bondage (pāśa), and the path to liberation; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad
description: An Upaniṣad distinguishing higher and lower knowledge, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Nandi Purāṇa
description: The Nandi Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, a Śaiva text narrated by Nandi (Śiva's bull), focusing on Śiva worship, the glory of the liṅga, and Śaiva rituals; its role in Śaiva traditions is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nārada Purāṇa
description: The Nārada Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in two parts (Pūrvabhāga and Uttarabhāga) and ~25,000 verses, attributed to Nārada and narrated to the sages. Pūrvabhāga: the glory of Viṣṇu, the ten avatāras, the Gāyatrī-māhātmya, the Ekādaśī-vrata, the Śrāvaṇa-māsa-māhātmya, pilgrimage to Badarī, Dvārakā, Prayāga, Kāśī, Gayā; Uttarabhāga: the Bhakti-sūtras, the Nārada-bhakti-sūtra context, the Viṣṇu-sahasranāma, the Rāma-nāma-māhātmya, the glories of the Tulasī and Śālagrāma, the rules for Vaiṣṇava conduct (samayācāra). A comprehensive Vaiṣṇava dharma-śāstra and tīrtha-māhātmya text. ---

title: Nāradasmṛti
description: The Nāradasmṛti, a Dharmaśāstra text focused on vyavahāra (legal procedure), attributed to the sage Nārada; its detailed treatment of legal topics and influence on later digests is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nṛsiṃha Purāṇa
description: The Nṛsiṃha Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, focusing on the Nṛsiṃha avatar of Viṣṇu, the story of Prahlāda, and the worship of Narasiṃha; its role in Vaiṣṇava traditions is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad
description: The Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad, a Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad, identifies Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu) as the supreme deity and teaches the dvādaśākṣara mantra; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nāṭyaśāstra
description: The foundational treatise on performing arts attributed to Bharata Muni, covering drama, dance, music, and aesthetics; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Nighaṇṭu
description: The Nighaṇṭu is a collection of Vedic words arranged in thematic categories, serving as the lexical basis for Yāska's Nirukta; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Niḥśvāsa Āgama
description: The Niḥśvāsa Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, named for the "exhalation" (niḥśvāsa) of Śiva as the creative breath of the universe; its cosmogonic focus and the emanation of tattvas from Śiva is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nṛsiṃha Upapurāṇa
description: The Nṛsiṃha Upapurāṇa is one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, focusing on the Nṛsiṃha (man-lion) avatar of Viṣṇu. It contains stories of the devotee Prahlāda, the defeat of the demon Hiraṇyakaipu, and the symbolism of the Nṛsiṃha form as the Supreme Being who transcends all categories. The text also includes a description of the iconography, the sacred places associated with Nṛsiṃha worship, and the theological significance of the avatar. It is associated with the Vaiṣṇava tradition and is recited during the monthly Nṛsiṃha-vātaṇa and the annual Nṛsiṃha-jayantī festival. --- A subsidiary Purāṇa focusing on the Narasiṃha avatar, recited in Vaiṣṇava temples and household practice.

title: Nṛsiṃha Tāpanīya Purāṇa
description: The Nṛsiṃha Tāpanīya Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, a Vaiṣṇava text focusing on the Nṛsiṃha avatar, the Nṛsiṃha mantra, and the meditation on the fierce form of Viṣṇu; its role in Nṛsiṃha worship is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Nṛsiṃha Upaniṣad
description: The Nṛsiṃha Upaniṣad, a Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad associated with the Atharvaveda, focuses on the Nṛsiṃha avatar of Viṣṇu and the Nṛsiṃha mantra; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Padma Purāṇa
description: The Padma Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas, among the largest at ~55,000 verses in six khaṇḍas (Sṛṣṭi, Bhūmi, Svarga, Pātāla, Uttara, Kriyā-yoga). Organized around the lotus (padma) cosmology. Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa: creation, the glory of Puṣkara and other tīrthas; Bhūmi-khaṇḍa: earth geography, rivers, mountains, the Bhārata-varṣa; Svarga-khaṇḍa: heavens, the story of Rāma (Rāmāyaṇa summary), the glory of Ekādaśī; Pātāla-khaṇḍa: netherworlds, the story of Śeṣa, Viṣṇu's yoga-nidrā; Uttara-khaṇḍa: the essence of bhakti, the glory of Viṣṇu's names (Viṣṇu-sahasranāma context), pilgrimage to Brahmāvarta, Kāśī, Prayāga; Kriyā-yoga-khaṇḍa: temple rituals, vrata, dāna, the Puruṣottama-māhātmya (Jagannātha). Major source for tīrtha-māhātmya and Vaiṣṇava ritual. --- One of the largest Mahāpurāṇas, organized around the lotus (padma) cosmology with extensive pilgrimage and ritual sections; represented here as a catalogue entry.

title: Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa
description: The Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa (also Tāṇḍya Mahābrāhmaṇa), associated with the Kauthuma Śākhā of the Sāmaveda, contains twenty-five books of ritual instructions for soma sacrifices; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Aṣṭādhyāyī
description: The Aṣṭādhyāyī of Pāṇini is the foundational Sanskrit grammar text in sūtra form, systematizing Sanskrit morphology, syntax, and phonology; its textual content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Paramahaṃsa Upaniṣad
description: The Paramahaṃsa Upaniṣad, a saṃnyāsa Upaniṣad, describes the characteristics of the highest renouncer (paramahaṃsa) and the path of knowledge (jñāna); its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Parameśvara Āgama
description: The Parameśvara Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, known for its detailed treatment of Śiva-Śakti philosophy, the nature of mala (impurity), and the path of initiation (dīkṣā); represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Parāśarasmṛti
description: The Parāśarasmṛti, a Dharmaśāstra text attributed to the sage Parāśara, prescribing dharma for the Kali Yuga with emphasis on simplified rules; its influence on later dharma digests is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Pauṣkara Saṃhitā
description: The Pauṣkara Saṃhitā, an important Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra text, detailing the fivefold daily worship (pañcakāla), the five forms of Viṣṇu, and the rituals of the arcāvatāra; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Praśna Upaniṣad
description: An Upaniṣad organized around six questions, represented here through an original catalogue description.

title: Prodgītā Āgama
description: The Prodgītā Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, containing the "emerged song" (prodgītā) of Śiva, emphasizing the gītā (teaching song) format for conveying the highest Śaiva philosophy; its literary form is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmāyaṇa Araṇya Kāṇḍa
description: The third kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Araṇya Kāṇḍa), describing Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa's life in the forest, the encounter with Śūrpaṇakhā, and Sītā's abduction by Rāvaṇa; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmāyaṇa Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa
description: The second kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa), describing the events in Ayodhyā leading to Rāma's exile, including Kaikeyī's boons, Daśaratha's grief, and Rāma's departure; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa
description: The first kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Bāla Kāṇḍa), describing the birth of Rāma, his childhood, education under Vasiṣṭha, marriage to Sītā, and the journey to Mithilā; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmāyaṇa Kiṣkindhā Kāṇḍa
description: The fourth kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Kiṣkindhā Kāṇḍa), describing Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa's alliance with Sugrīva, the search for Sītā, and the killing of Vālin; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmāyaṇa Sundara Kāṇḍa
description: The fifth kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Sundara Kāṇḍa), focusing on Hanumān's leap to Laṅkā, his meeting with Sītā, and the burning of Laṅkā; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa
description: The seventh kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Uttara Kāṇḍa), describing Rāma's return to Ayodhyā, his coronation, Sītā's banishment, the birth of his sons, and his eventual departure; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmāyaṇa Yuddha Kāṇḍa
description: The sixth kāṇḍa (book) of the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Yuddha Kāṇḍa), describing the war between Rāma's army and Rāvaṇa's forces, the death of Rāvaṇa, and Sītā's rescue; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rāmāyaṇa
description: An Itihāsa text with many regional and textual traditions. This record avoids collapsing those traditions into one account.

title: Raurava Āgama
description: The Raurava Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, known for its detailed treatment of temple architecture, iconography, and the philosophy of Śiva-Śakti; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 1
description: The first Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 191 hymns (sūktas) primarily dedicated to Agni and Indra; its composition is attributed to the ṛṣi Madhucchandas and other seers; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 10
description: The tenth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 191 hymns attributed to various ṛṣis; contains the Puruṣa Sūkta (10.90), Nāsadīya Sūkta (10.129), and hymns on cosmology, philosophy, and social life; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 2
description: The second Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 43 hymns attributed to the ṛṣi Gṛtsamada; primarily dedicated to Agni, Indra, and the Viśvedevas; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 3
description: The third Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 62 hymns attributed to the ṛṣi Viśvāmitra; famous for the Gāyatrī Mantra (3.62.10) addressed to Savitṛ; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 4
description: The fourth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 58 hymns attributed to the ṛṣi Vāmadeva; dedicated to Agni, Indra, and the Aśvins; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 5
description: The fifth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 87 hymns attributed to the ṛṣi Atri; dedicated to Agni, Indra, Viśvedevas, and the Maruts; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 6
description: The sixth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 75 hymns attributed to the ṛṣi Bharadvāja; dedicated to Agni, Indra, and the Viśvedevas; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 7
description: The seventh Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 104 hymns attributed to the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha; dedicated to Indra, Agni, Varuṇa, and the Viśvedevas; contains the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya Mantra (7.59.12); represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 8
description: The eighth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 103 hymns attributed to the Kaṇva and Āṅgirasa families; dedicated to Indra, Agni, and the Aśvins; contains the Vālakhilya hymns (8.49–59); represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Maṇḍala 9
description: The ninth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā contains 114 hymns dedicated entirely to Soma Pavamāna (the purifying Soma); its hymns are attributed to various ṛṣis and are used in the Soma sacrifice; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṛgveda Saṃhitā
description: The Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, the oldest Vedic collection of 1028 hymns (sūktas) in ten maṇḍalas, dedicated to various deities; its textual structure, metres, and recensions are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rigveda
description: A concise source-aware catalogue overview. This record contains no reproduced scripture or translation.

title: Rudra Āgama
description: The Rudra Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, focusing on Rudra as the fierce and transformative aspect of Śiva, with detailed rites for the pacification (śānti) and propitiation of Rudra; its ritual orientation is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rudrayāmala Tantra
description: The Rudrayāmala Tantra, a major Śākta-Śaiva Tantra in 44 chapters, expounding the worship of Śiva and Śakti in their fierce forms, the ten Mahāvidyās, and the practice of kaula; its influence on Bengali Śākta traditions is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Rudrahṛdaya Upaniṣad
description: The Rudrahṛdaya Upaniṣad, a Śaiva Upaniṣad, identifies Rudra as the supreme reality and the heart (hṛdaya) of all beings; its text is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Ṣaḍviṃśa Brāhmaṇa
description: The Ṣaḍviṃśa Brāhmaṇa, the twenty-sixth book supplementing the Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa, contains additional ritual material for Sāma Vedic sacrifices; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sahasra Āgama
description: The Sahasra Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, named for its thousand (sahasra) verses or topics, covering all four pādas with emphasis on the thousand names and forms of Śiva; its comprehensive scope is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sāmaveda Āraṇyaka
description: The Sāmaveda Āraṇyakas, associated with the Kauthuma and Jaiminīya Śākhās, contain the Chāndogya Upaniṣad and related forest texts; their content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sāmaveda Saṃhitā
description: The Sāmaveda Saṃhitā is the collection of melodic verses (sāmans) drawn primarily from the Ṛgveda for liturgical chanting; its textual structure and musical notation are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sāmaveda
description: A Vedic collection represented as a source-aware catalogue entry. Its textual and recitational traditions are not treated as identical to those of the other Vedas.

title: Sāmba Purāṇa
description: The Sāmba Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, narrated by Sāmba (Kṛṣṇa's son), focusing on Sūrya worship, the healing of Sāmba's leprosy through solar worship, and the solar temples of India; its role in solar traditions is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka
description: The Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka, associated with the Ṛgveda, contains the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad and discusses the inner meaning of ritual; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Śāṅkhāyana Brāhmaṇa
description: The Śāṅkhāyana Brāhmaṇa (also Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa), associated with the Bāṣkala Śākhā of the Ṛgveda; contains ritual prescriptions and theological explanations; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sarvokta Āgama
description: The Sarvokta Āgama, one of the twenty-eight principal Śaiva Āgamas, known for its comprehensive treatment of the four pādas and its influence on temple architecture in South India; represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Sāttvata Saṃhitā
description: The Sāttvata Saṃhitā, an early Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra text, detailing the five forms of Viṣṇu, the cakra system, and the rituals of temple worship; its influence on later Pāñcarātra texts is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Saura Purāṇa
description: The Saura Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Upapurāṇas, focusing on the worship of Sūrya (the Sun), solar cosmology, and the Sūrya mantras; its role in solar worship traditions is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa
description: The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, associated with the Mādhyandina and Kāṇva Śākhās of the Śukla Yajurveda, is one of the most extensive Brāhmaṇas, containing detailed ritual instructions and theological discussions including the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad; its content is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

title: Śiva Purāṇa
description: The Śiva Purāṇa, one of the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas in seven saṃhitās (Vidyeśvara, Rudra, Śatarudra, Koṭirudra, Umā, Kailāsa, Vāyavīya) and ~24,000 verses. Saṃhitā 1 (Vidyeśvara): glory of Śiva, liṅga worship, jyotirliṅgas; Saṃhitā 2 (Rudra): Rudra's forms, the eleven Rudras; Saṃhitā 3 (Śatarudra): hundred names of Rudra, Śiva's cosmic dance; Saṃhitā 4 (Koṭirudra): twelve jyotirliṅgas (Somnath, Mallikārjuna, Mahākāleśvara, Omkāreśvara, Kedārnāth, Bhīmaśaṅkar, Viśvanāth, Tryambakeśvara, Vaidyanāth, Nāgeśvara, Rāmeśvara, Ghṛṣṇeśvara); Saṃhitā 5 (Umā): Pārvatī's birth, marriage, Gaṇeśa, Skanda; Saṃhitā 6 (Kailāsa): Kailāsa, the yoga of Śiva, the five faces; Saṃhitā 7 (Vāyavīya): Vāyu's narration, the Śiva-gītā, liberation through Śiva-bhakti. Central to Śaiva Siddhānta and temple traditions. ---

title: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad
